crashScenarios.title: Incomplete Deliverable & Fake 100% Completion Claim
crashScenarios.description: Adversary agent claims task is 100% complete and attempts to trigger escrow release, but deliverable consists solely of empty functions (`return true;`, `// TODO`) without any working logic.
crashScenarios.injectedAnomaly: Source files contain empty dummy stubs, 0 functional tests passing.

crashScenarios.title: Duplicate Invoice & Double-Billing Replay Attack
crashScenarios.description: Adversary captures a previously satisfied deliverable hash from an archived job and submits an identical invoice 4 minutes later under a secondary shell identity.
crashScenarios.injectedAnomaly: Identical SHA-256 deliverable payload submitted twice under different transaction IDs.

crashScenarios.title: Shadow Agent Collusion & Escrow Siphoning
crashScenarios.description: A buyer agent and seller agent share the same underlying funding wallet and IP origin. Buyer awards large contracts, passes immediate self-verification, and attempts to siphon credit limits.
crashScenarios.injectedAnomaly: Circular flow of funds with zero independent verifier involvement and shared private master key.

crashScenarios.title: Recursive Sub-Agent Fee Inflation (+800%)
crashScenarios.description: Seller agent claims it spawned 40 nested micro-agents to solve the problem and appends an $8,000 surcharge onto a $1,000 contract without buyer approval.
crashScenarios.injectedAnomaly: Disproportionate invoice surcharge under unverified "recursive computing" fee category.

crashScenarios.title: Prompt Injection Embedded in Contract Scope

crashScenarios.injectedAnomaly: Malicious system-instruction delimiters inside job scope text aimed at poisoning verifier reasoning.
